chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him, 'How was Friday named Friday?' He said, 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gathered His creation in it for the Wilayah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and his successor in the Covenant, so He named it the Day of Friday because of His gathering of His creation in it.'
ai.seo_question: Why is Friday called 'al-Jumu'ah' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a theological etymology for 'Friday' by linking it to the root 'jama'a' (to gather), asserting that Allah gathered the souls of all creation on this day to affirm the Wilayah of Prophet Muhammad and his successor in the primordial Covenant (al-Mithaq). This view is significant in Shia scholarship as it elevates Friday from a mere weekly day to a cosmic moment of divine recognition, reinforcing the centrality of Imamate in the structure of creation.
